newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Congress studies gasoline competition.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Congress studies gasoline competition.

text.p: Venezuela's Senate Energy and Mines Comittee received Tuesday a government plan to reform the country's gasoline market and allow foreign oil companies to compete for motorists' business, it said in a statement.
The new law is a key part of Venezuela's oil "apertura" or opening, which also involves foreign oil companies participating in the exploration and production of Venezuelan crude oil.
The domestic gasoline and diesel market runs to about about 350,000 barrels per day and liberalisation has already attracted the interest of international oil giants Mobil, Texaco and Shell.
Most petrol stations are already owned privately, but the supply of refined products is a monopoly of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) and the government sets prices well below cost.

The government's proposal would provide for a year's transition period, when prices would rise to the factory gate level and the government would continue to pay retailers a profit margin. After a year, all price controls would disappear.
The law would also liberalise the transport of fuels from refineries to service stations, currently a tightly controlled business where the government fixes tariffs.
The government would continue to have a regulating role under the plan, checking that new entrants comply to the quality rules and other regulations.
The government's proposal may still go through many changes, because it is up against a competing, more conservative plan put forward by a small group of legislators.
